findings.title: Unhealthy flusher processes are no longer killed before being replaced.
findings.body:
The old code always called `self.process.kill()` before it restarted the flusher. The new code only kills when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is true. The processes come from `mp_context.Process` with the `spawn` context, so they are `SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so this check is always false in production.

When a flusher hangs (the `hang` cause), it keeps running and a second process is started for the same shards. Both then flush and produce the same segments at the same time, which can produce duplicates or break each other's flush bookkeeping. Each later restart adds another leaked process.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or test for a `kill` attribute instead.

findings.title: join() stops before terminating the remaining processes once the deadline passes, and its terminate check never matches spawned processes.
findings.body:
When the deadline expires, `break` leaves the loop, so no process after that point gets `terminate()`. The old code always reached the terminate step after its wait.

Separately, `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is false for `SpawnProcess`, so `terminate()` is skipped for every process anyway.

Result: on a rebalance or shutdown with a timeout, flusher processes for the old partition assignment can keep running and flushing shards that now belong to another consumer.

Fix: wait until the deadline, then terminate every process that is still alive, using `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` in the type check.

findings.title: The metric tag key here is "shards", but the sibling metrics use "shard".
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `shard`. Dashboards that filter or group by `shard` will miss this metric. Use the same key everywhere.
